title: Dynamic Localisation of Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network

problem.claim: Adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural networks provide accurate data-driven modelling of spatial-temporal dependencies but impose increased computational demands.

gap.claim: Existing adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural networks do not account for spatial dependencies that dynamically evolve over time.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces DynAGS, a localised adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural network framework for distributed deployment.
DynAGS combines dynamic localisation, time-evolving spatial graphs, and personalised localisation through a lightweight central Dynamic Graph Generator using cross attention.
The framework generates dynamic sparse graphs from node feature representations without costly data exchanges and supports personalised localisation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across two core adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural network architectures and nine real-world datasets, DynAGS outperforms current benchmarks.
The authors report that dynamic modelling of spatial dependencies improves model expressibility, flexibility, and system efficiency, particularly in distributed settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial-temporal data contains dependencies linking current measurements with historical measurements across locations.
Adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural networks model these dependencies using data-driven rather than predefined spatial graphs.
The data-driven approach improves accuracy but increases computational demands.
DynAGS addresses the challenge with dynamic localisation, time-evolving spatial graphs, personalised localisation, and a cross-attention-based Dynamic Graph Generator.
Experiments on two architectures and nine real-world datasets are reported to outperform current benchmarks and improve expressibility, flexibility, and efficiency.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the nine datasets or report quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, deployment topology, or computational cost.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or comparisons across individual DynAGS components.
